strengths: Large-scale, well-curated dataset (489K + 165K) addressing genuine gaps in visual reasoning supervision (limited multi-round CoT, 2D-only annotations)
Thoughtful dataset design with adaptive multi-round zoom strategy, clear annotation format, and systematic global-to-local reasoning supervision
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple benchmarks (Visual-CoT, MME, V*Bench) with strong results and thorough ablation studies
Novel depth-aware supervision through monocular depth and semantic segmentation, extending beyond prior 2D-only approaches
Excellent reproducibility with detailed implementation specs, training configurations, algorithms, and prompt examples in appendix
Broad domain coverage (text/doc, fine-grained, general VQA, spatial reasoning) with good annotation quality and human evaluation results
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: training approach is standard SFT with LoRA; contribution is primarily dataset curation and scale rather than methodological innovation

Pseudo-3D annotation quality concerns: monocular depth is inherently uncertain; no ground-truth validation; impact of depth errors on reasoning not quantified; unclear if noisy depth supervision helps most tasks

Heavy GPT-4 dependence for annotations introduces bias, reproducibility concerns, and questions about whether models learn visual reasoning or GPT reasoning patterns; minimal inter-annotator agreement discussion

Unfair baseline comparisons: VISREASON models benefit from iterative multi-round zoom while baselines use single-step prediction; should either fine-tune all baselines on equivalent data or isolate dataset effect
Weak 3D grounding performance (0.276 grounded ratio) suggests models struggle with explicit grounding despite depth supervision; limited failure analysis of why grounding remains challenging
Insufficient ablation of depth contribution: no clear isolation of value from depth vs. better rationales; unclear which tasks benefit from 3D supervision; missing per-domain analysis
Very limited human evaluation (30 raters × 20 examples = 600 annotations for 489K dataset) without inter-rater agreement metrics or statistical significance testing
Dataset heavily derived from Visual-CoT (limited novelty in source); modest improvements on external benchmarks (MME: 0.777 vs. InternVL 0.848) suggest limited generalization and transfer

strengths: Large-scale, multi-domain dataset (489K + 165K examples) addressing real gaps in visual CoT resources: scale, multi-round supervision, and depth-aware spatial reasoning
Thoughtful annotation design with global-to-local workflow reflecting human visual reasoning; adaptive zoom-in strategy preserves efficiency
Rigorous validation: comprehensive human audit (2,200 examples with confidence intervals), calibrated automatic evaluator (r=0.758), user study with 30 raters, multiple evaluation suites
Technically sound methodology with clear algorithms, proper coordinate transformations, and principled iterative refinement strategy
Strong improvements on targeted tasks: fine-grained recognition (+0.150 on CUB), spatial reasoning (+0.307 on Open Images), consistent ablation validation
Comprehensive supplementary material enabling reproducibility: all prompts, training configurations, implementation details, human audit results
Honest discussion of limitations including cascading localization failures, rationale quality issues, pseudo-depth noise, and Text/Doc performance trade-offs
weaknesses: Cascading localization errors remain unresolved: no recovery mechanism when initial RoI misalignment traps reasoning in irrelevant regions; no quantification of failure frequency or impact

Domain-specific gains, not universal transfer: Text/Doc performance degrades (0.920→0.892), source-removal ablation reveals massive dependency on domain-relevant training data, InternVL transfer shows mixed results (improvements on CUB/Open Images but degradation on GQA, Visual7W, VSR)
Rationale quality concerns: only 86.5% necessity and faithfulness in audit; Text/Doc particularly weak (70.9%, 71.9%); acknowledged mismatch between local crops and global reasoning requirements
Pseudo-depth labeled as '3D-grounding' but provides only ordinal cues from noisy monocular estimation; no analysis of error propagation; coordinate re-normalization under cropping under-specified
Heavy dependence on GPT-4.1-series for annotation generation creates circular reasoning bias and potential LLM artifacts; variability between VisReason (4.1-Nano) and VisReason-Pro (4.1-Mini)
Computational cost of multi-round inference not addressed; no timing comparisons despite clear efficiency trade-off; practical applicability limited despite accuracy gains
Limited failure mode analysis beyond cascading errors; no systematic error categorization; second-backbone transfer shows inconsistent generalization across tasks
Evaluation format mismatch (multi-round vs. direct-QA) suggests improvements may be format-specific rather than representing genuine reasoning capability gains
